profile.address: Beech Road Southwest, New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, 43062
profile.reading: This building (OSM-tagged "NAO 3") is part of Meta's New Albany data center campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, just east of Columbus. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and, per its own fact sheet, has invested more than $1.5 billion in the campus, employs 300-plus people once complete, drew 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and has provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Franklin- and Licking County-area schools and nonprofits, alongside its usual LEED Gold, net-zero, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Real-estate and land-acquisition reporting sourced from county deed records shows Meta, operating through its Sidecat LLC affiliate, has assembled 1,345 acres across 18 parcels in Licking County since an initial 1.3-acre purchase in October 2017, with $679 million spent on land alone; a 2025 round of purchases covering 514 acres cost $566 million, pushing per-acre land prices above $1.1 million as the campus expanded aggressively. AEP Ohio has said it is building two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically to serve the site, and state utility filings describe a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for construction directly on the campus, targeting completion in 2026, so Meta can power part of the expansion independently of the regional grid. Local and regional reporting (Spectrum News 1, News 5 Cleveland) describes the expanded campus as a "gigawatt-scale" data center, with an Ohio State University sustainability researcher estimating its electricity draw at roughly the equivalent of 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers, and construction employing thousands of workers across the region even though permanent staffing is comparatively small relative to the facility's power draw. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual New Albany structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Licking County's New Albany area has become, per News 5 Cleveland, one of the starting points of Ohio's broader data center boom, with Microsoft and Google facilities also sited nearby and Cologix separately reported to be planning a large Licking County campus of its own. Community advocacy groups such as Stop Ohio Data Centers have organized around concerns over the sector's land use, water use, and grid impact in the New Albany/Licking County corridor, while state and AEP Ohio utility filings document the scale of dedicated transmission and generation infrastructure being built to serve Meta's campus specifically.

reading.body:
Meta's New Albany campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, is a gigawatt-scale expansion that has assembled 1,345 acres across 18 parcels since 2017, with $679 million spent on land alone and $1.5 billion invested overall by the operator. The campus is not published with per-building capacity figures, confirmed building count, or exact square footage; regional reporting and an Ohio State University sustainability researcher estimate the expanded facility's electricity draw at roughly equivalent to 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers. NAO 3, the mapped building identified here, is one structure within this larger campus cluster.

The scale of dedicated power infrastructure being built to serve this site signals its importance to AI deployment. AEP Ohio is constructing two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically for the campus, and state utility filings describe a 200-megawatt on-site natural gas plant approved for construction and targeting 2026 completion, allowing Meta to supply part of the expansion independently of the regional grid. The commitment to build generation capacity directly on campus, rather than relying solely on grid connection, reflects the site's projected load and Meta's assessment that regional grid supply cannot meet it alone.

New Albany has become one of Ohio's primary data center anchors, with Microsoft and Google facilities sited nearby and Cologix reportedly planning a large campus of its own in Licking County. Of 76 data center facilities mapped in Ohio, only 8 operators publish megawatt figures, totaling 60.4 MW; Meta's New Albany campus is not ranked in that published total because no per-building or campus-wide IT capacity figure is disclosed by the operator. The site's gigawatt-scale footprint and dedicated transmission and generation infrastructure mean it likely represents one of the largest unpublished capacity clusters in the state and a binding constraint on the regional grid.
